stories.title: SSGC announces winter gas supply schedule for Sindh, Balochistan
summary: KARACHI: The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) on Wednesday announced the gas supply schedule for the winter season, under which three slots have been fixed for supply to domestic consumers, in line with federal government directives.

Gas availability under new schedule: 6:30am-9am (Breakfast) 12pm-2:30pm (Lunch) 6pm-9pm (Dinner) The SSGC shared the schedule on its website and social media platforms, saying that it was “prioritising domestic consumers by ensuring supply during meal times”.
For the past some years, SSGC’s consumers have not been getting round-the-clock gas supply.

stories.title: US midterms: Democrats win US Congress in midterm rout of Trump
summary: Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office.
In California, Democrat Xavier Becerra handily defeated Donald Trump-backed Republican Steve Hilton in the race to become the governor, US networks said.

Democrats held onto three House districts in Florida that Republican lawmakers had redrawn earlier this year, all of which backed Trump by at least nine percentage points, according to media projections.

stories.title: Israel election commission rejects Netanyahu charges of fraud
summary: Israeli electoral authorities on Wednesday rejected allegations promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fraud by Arab parties, who could hold the key to removing him from power after a divisive vote.

President Isaac Herzog will at noon (1000 GMT) officially receive the results of the October 27 election as he decides whether to give Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, with neither commanding enough votes alone.

He had earlier warned Netanyahu against launching a new war with his close ally US President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli prime minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.

stories.title: 'We did it!': Democrat El-Sayed hails US Senate win, becomes first Muslim elected to upper chamber of Congress
summary: During the race, El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas.
The victory made El-Sayed the first Democratic doctor in the Senate since 1969. “Everybody in politics is so trash.
Addressing the vice president, El-Sayed said in his victory speech “you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January”.

stories.title: Historic leadership firsts for minorities across US in midterm vote
summary: The first Black female governor, the first openly gay male senator and the first female Native American governor all won groundbreaking elections in the vote that racked up resounding wins for Democrats.
Democratic Representative Chris Pappas, meanwhile, will become the first openly gay man to serve in the US Senate after winning in New Hampshire.
The sweeping midterm rebuke of Trump also saw a number of state-level electoral firsts, including the first Latina governor in Texas with Gina Hinojosa’s victory.

stories.title: Numbers that tell the story of the Democrats' midterm blowout
summary: Young voters, Latinos turn away Young men and Latino voters — two segments of the American electorate crucial to Trump — turned sharply away from the president and his Republican Party, exit polls showed.

Hispanic voters had helped bring Trump to power in 2016, and were instrumental in his victory in 2024, when they only narrowly went to Democrat Kamala Harris in the presidential election, 51 per cent to 48pc, according to Pew Research.
It showed in NBC News exit polls on Tuesday, when Latino voters backed Democratic candidates by 62pc to 35pc over Republicans.

stories.title: Dashain gone, Tihar uncertain: Nepali workers stranded in Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks disrupt flights
summary: Similarly, Etihad Airways has cancelled some flights from Abu Dhabi to Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until November 5.
Qatar Airways has suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam and reduced the number of services to Jeddah.
However, no new dates have been announced for the resumption of flights to Riyadh and Dammam following October 24.

stories.title: Democratic takeover of US Congress: What happens next
summary: Democrats are preparing a legislative offensive against US President Donald Trump after their sweeping midterm victory handed them control of both chambers of Congress and the power to challenge his policies, investigate his administration and block his nominees.
Trump retains his veto, while Senate rules allow Republicans to obstruct most legislation.
Democrats could pursue Trump’s third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so.

stories.title: Pakistan's Maliha Ali topples Russia's Drozdova at MMA world championships
summary: Maliha Ali defeated Veronika Drozdova, a two-time European champion and, at 19, by split decision in their featherweight (65.8kg) bout at the world championships of amateur mixed martial arts.
Maliha, who is also a wushu champion and a national kickboxing gold medallist, came into the tournament off a silver medal at the IMMAF World Cup in Angola earlier this year.
The round went to the Russian, but the first two belonged to Maliha.

stories.title: Lone Star turns blue: Democrats Talarico, Hinojosa topple Texas Republicans
summary: Talarico defeated the state’s attorney general Ken Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump who was heavily backed by tech billionaire Elon Musk, US media projected.

The result was a major setback for Trump, who threw his weight behind Paxton and made the state a campaign priority. “We defeated Goliath,” Talarico told a victory rally in Austin, the state capital. “In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths.
Talarico and Hinojosa are the first Democrats to win statewide office in Texas since 1994.

stories.title: Teachers in Peshawar protest ‘abrupt layoffs’ by UNHCR
summary: PESHAWAR: Hundreds of Pakistani teachers, who provided education to Afghan children in refugee camps for decades, but were laid off without any financial relief, protested here on Tuesday against the ‘abrupt’ layoffs.

As many as 291 teachers, who have been providing education to Afghan children under the auspices of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) for the past 35 to 40 years, have been laid off without prior notice or any financial relief.
The dismissed teachers demanded compensation and financial relief for their decades of service.

stories.title: Seminary teacher held for beating student to death in KP's Bajaur
summary: BAJAUR: Police have arrested a seminary teacher for allegedly beating a student to death in Bajaur district, officials said on Tuesday.

They added that the teacher of a seminary in the Qazafi Bandagi area of Utmankhel tehsil, who had fled after allegedly beating his student to death inside the madressah, was arrested during a raid conducted after the incident came to light.
A team from Utmankhel police station, led by District Police Officer Khan Zeb Mohmand, arrested him during a raid, according to a statement.

stories.title: Fazl hints at launching street agitation
summary: Says JUI-F will not allow govt to plunder natural resources You must stand firm against oppression and adversity, as activists of no other party dare to stand up at this critical juncture,” he said.
He said that the government shouldn’t cross its limits to compel JUI-F workers to come forward for the security of Maulana Fazlur Rahman. “We don’t want to take law into our hands.

Speaking on the occasion, provincial office-bearers of JUI-F Maulana Nasir Mehmood, Malik Waheed and Malik Naveed said that workers of the party were ready to stand shoulder to shoulder with their leader Maulana Fazlur Rahman in his fight for the rights of people.

stories.title: School in Sindh's Kandhkot village set to open after years of lawlessness
summary: Larkana Commissioner Dr Rasheed Masood Khan chaired a meeting of senior government officials in the office of the Kandhkot-Kashmore deputy commissioner to discuss the socio-economic development of the riverine areas.

Speaking on the occasion, DIG Shiraz said that peace had been restored in the riverine areas as a result of the Sindh government’s ‘surrender policy’ for criminals and the joint efforts made by all law enforcement agencies.
They noted that after the marked improvement in the law and order situation in the riverine areas of Kandhkot-Kashmore district, provision of basic facilities to people had begun.

stories.title: Sindh cabinet approves new price of wheat at Rs4,500 per 40kg
summary: KARACHI: The Sindh cabinet on Tuesday approved a Rs500 cut in the wheat release price from Rs5,000 to Rs4,500 per 40kg following a dip in market prices.
Addressing a press conference after the cabinet meeting, Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon said that the decision would bring down the price of flour by Rs15 per kg.

It said that the cabinet approved the processing of 1,275 acres of state land in Dehs Bakran and Pipri, District Malir, for establishing an industrial park on a government-to-government basis, utilising land associated with Pakistan Steel Mills (PSM) to boost industrialisation.

stories.title: New IO given 10 days to complete Mir Raza murder probe
summary: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday granted an additional 10 days to the newly appointed investigation officer (IO) to complete the probe into the Mir Raza murder case.

A day earlier, the court had issued a show-cause notice to the head of the joint investigation team (JIT), police officer Irfan Baloch, and sought his response over the police failure to submit the final charge sheet in the case.
After hearing the investigation officer, the court granted him an additional 10 days to complete the probe.

stories.title: Lahore Gymkhana suspends member over ‘hooliganism’ at club
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore Gymkhana Club administration has suspended the membership of a son of an “influential member” following his alleged involvement in hooliganism in the club, forming a three-member committee to probe the matter.

Justifying the action, club chairman Salman Saddique told Dawn that the membership suspension is a standard operating procedure (SOP) in case of any serious breach of discipline by a Gymkhana member, whether inside or outside the club.
He said that as per standard procedure, a three-member standing discipline committee, comprising independent senior club members, is looking into the scuffle issue.

stories.title: Punjab govt's Chronic Myeloid Leukemia programme: Supply disruption forces patients to get drugs from market
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab government’s life-saving mega Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) programme suffered a major setback due to three-month-long disruption in distribution of cancer drugs to the critical patients in five designated centres across the province.

Five centres unable to provide free cancer medicines due to prolonged delay in bidding process; minister says dept trying to make drugs available Following the grave situation, most of the patients were bearing additional expenses.
Since then, he said, it was distributing free cancer drugs to the patients at the registered centres.

stories.title: HEC can’t deal with employment matters of varsities: LHC
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Tuesday held that the Higher Education Commission (HEC) does not have the power to deal with the service matters of the faculty or employees of chartered universities in Pakistan.
Justice Jawad Hassan was hearing a petition by a private university challenging an HEC order that allegedly issued certain directions about its affairs.
Justice Hassan suspended the impugned HEC order, observing that the university’s argument that the commission exceeded its jurisdiction “appears to carry considerable weight”.

stories.title: Man held on blasphemy charges in Gujrat
summary: A local trader of Kotla Main Bazaar alleged in his complaint lodged with the Kakrali Police Station that the suspect, a resident of Chakanwali village, arrived in a local mosque after the Asr prayers and asked the worshippers to listen to him.
ENCOUNTERS: The suspect who stabbed a 12-year-old boy some days ago was killed during an alleged encounter in Gujranwala.
A spokesman for Gujranwala police said Sajjad Hussain was arrested for stabbing the motorcyclist boy, Abdullah, in a bid to snatch his motorbike on Oct 30 in the Saddar police area.

stories.title: Lahore basant preparations reviewed: Kite flying to be strictly restricted to designated areas
summary: Assistant Commissioner (HR) Waqas Anjum, representatives of kite-flying associations and other administrative and police officials also attended the meeting.

Mr Ahmed said the participation of lower-income groups in the festival would be ensured, adding that licensed kite-flying permit holders would be allowed to operate freely while adhering to the prescribed rules and regulations.

The DIG said stringent security arrangements would remain in place before, during and after the festival, as in Basant 2026, as the authorities are determined to ensure peaceful celebrations in 2027 as well.

summary: Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz also held a separate meeting with Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir to discuss the overall situation in the country, a source in the Prime Minister’s Office told Dawn.
When contacted, a source privy to the meeting said it was a long-overdue meeting with the prime minister, during which the situation in all provinces was discussed.
Similarly, Balochistan Governor Sarfraz Bugti apprised the meeting of the security situation in his province.

stories.title: Journalists observe Black Day in Balochistan
summary: Black flags were hoisted at all press clubs in the province and journalists wore black armbands and staged demonstrations to highlight growing challenges being faced by the media industry.
In Quetta, the Balochistan Union of Journalists (BUJ) organised a protest outside the Quetta Press Club, where a black flag was hoisted and a sit-in was held.
A large number of journalists, lawyers and civil society representatives attended the sit-in.

stories.title: Senate panel questions Balochistan dam projects
summary: QUETTA: A Senate subcommittee on Less Developed Areas has expressed serious concerns over rising costs, delays and potential adverse impacts of major dam projects in Balochistan, directing relevant authorities to conduct fresh assessments and submit detailed reports.

The meeting, chaired by Senator Jan Muhammad Baloch, was held in Islamabad, where officials from the Planning Commission and relevant departments briefed members on projects being implemented under the Aghaz-i-Haqooq-i-Balochistan Package.

The committee also questioned the sharp rise in the revised cost of Gish Kaur Storage Dam from Rs11bn to Rs44bn and asked the authorities to rea­ssess its financial viability and benefits for local residents.

stories.title: Inter cruise past Feyenoord
summary: Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike from German defender Yann Bisseck.
The three-time champions of Europe had lost their first two group games, but had far too much quality for a disappointing Feyenoord, who had little answer to Inter's pace and attacking ability.
Feyenoord's next Champions League encounter is a home tie against Porto, while Inter Milan welcome Stuttgart.

stories.title: Opposition nominees sought for election reforms panel
summary: Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry contacted PTI chief whip in the National Assembly Aamir Dogar, asking him to submit the names of opposition lawmakers for the committee.

The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), a major ally of the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N), has already approached opposition leaders Mehmood Khan Achakzai in the National Assembly and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas in the Senate, inviting them to join the proposed committee.

He urged the opposition to join the committee, saying the initiative could also pave the way for consultations on other important national issues, including the long-delayed appointment of a new chief election commissioner (CEC).

stories.title: Djokovic battles through Paris Masters opener
summary: Novak Djokovic battled from behind to beat Valentin Vacherot 6-7 (5/7), 7-5, 6-1 in the first round of the Paris Masters on Tuesday, while Ben Shelton opened his campaign with a comfortable win.

Djokovic also exacted his own bit of revenge on Vacherot in just the second meeting between the pair -- the Monegasque downed the 39-year-old on his way to a sensational Shanghai Masters title last season.

Vacherot then received treatment for a foot issue and soon found himself level at one set each as Djokovic displayed his trademark killer instinct to seize his first break opportunity in the 12th game of the set and send the match to a decider.

stories.title: PTI open to ‘joining hands’ with JUI-F
summary: PTI Secretary Gen­eral Salman Akram Raja told the media the party would welcome anyone who stood by the party and supported their struggle. “It is possible that some may walk with us for one mile, some for 10 miles and some till the end, but why should we reject them?” he said.

Meeting denied, again A day after Imran Kh­an’s lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar was allo­wed to meet the incarcerated PTI founder, the party claimed that members of Mr Khan’s family were again denied access to him, on Tuesday.

Advocate Chaudhry, whose name was also included in the list of lawyers who had to meet Mr Khan, said that lawyers including Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Salman Akram Raja, and Uzma Khanum’s son Abdullah Khan reached Adiala Jail, but they were not allowed to meet Mr Khan.

stories.title: Govt unveils LPG policy as power costs set to rise
summary: Under the base-case scenario, the power purchase price was projected at Rs27.31 per unit, an increase of Rs1.99.
Under the new arrangement, SOEs would import LPG in bulk and publish the base price, linked to the Saudi Aramco Contract Price.

Local producers would receive the producer price determined through auctions, while the difference between the producer price and the SOE-linked base price would be deposited in a fund to subsidise LPG for BISP-eligible consumers.

stories.title: Trump acknowledges Iran role in Democratic sweep
summary: President ​Donald Trump acknowledged that the war ‌in Iran played a role in Republicans' losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, as Democrats ​prepared to take control of ​both the US House and Senate ⁠and challenge his legislative agenda.
"Candidate quality matters, and President Trump did a better job promoting many of the candidates on the ballot than the candidates did themselves," a White House official said.
The question now is how Trump will react to being a lame duck president for the last two years of his second term, with Democrats in control of both the House and Senate.

stories.title: Abdul El-Sayed becomes 1st Muslim elected to US Senate in Michigan win
summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate after defeating former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in Michigan's closely watched race Tuesday, holding onto a crucial Democratic-held seat, according to projections by US media.
Political rise and historic Senate bid El-Sayed returned to electoral politics in 2026, defeating Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary in August.

Faith and political identity El-Sayed's Muslim identity also became a prominent issue during the Senate race, with President Donald Trump and other Republican figures repeatedly criticizing him over his faith and political positions.

stories.title: Pakistan's Test revival begins
summary: Pakistan have decided to put an end to their disappointing performances on lively pitches, with head coach Mike Hesson directing efforts to prepare pace-friendly surfaces for both home Test matches against Sri Lanka.
Following their triumph in the tri-nation ODI series, Pakistan's next assignment is a two-match Test series against Sri Lanka.
Remarkably, Pakistan will be playing their first home Test of the year in November, despite having already featured in seven Tests across three overseas series.

stories.title: Polio team supervisor abducted during vaccination drive in K-P's Jamrud
summary: A polio campaign team supervisor, identified as Jalil Khan, was abducted by unidentified armed men from the Chapri area of Jamrud in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) during the ongoing seven-day polio vaccination campaign, District Police Officer (DPO) Waqar Ahmad said on Wednesday.

Earlier in the week, four polio workers were abducted by unidentified armed men after being subjected to gunfire in K-P's Tank district, while two other members of a polio vaccination team, who had been kidnapped in Lower South Waziristan, were subsequently released.
In a separate incident, two members of a polio vaccination team were abducted by armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Lower South Waziristan.

stories.title: State land worth millions reclaimed in Swabi
summary: SWABI: Officials claim to have reclaimed state land worth millions of rupees, as an anti-encroachment operation continued across Swabi district the other day.
Encroachments have been removed along the Swabi-Jahangira Road in the district headquarters, and the Swabi-Mardan, Swabi-Topi and Swabi-Muneri roads.

The deputy commissioner said: “If a vendor is seen in front of a shop in the district headquarters or other markets, that shopkeeper will be arrested because he takes money from the vendor and allows him to stand in front of his outlet.” Published in Dawn, November 4th, 2026
